title: Wang et al. 2022: an aluminised 10 kg charge's reflected load at 1.2 m
summary: A bare 10 kg sphere of TNT, RDX and aluminium, which the paper gives as 10 kg of TNT, 0.7 m above the ground and 1.2 m from an upright steel plate (0.56 m/kg^(1/3)). The reflected peak, arrival and impulse at three gauges in the plate: a close-in load where the stated TNT equivalence is itself under test.

sources.title: Blast resistance of reinforced concrete slabs based on residual load-bearing capacity
sources.used_for: The charge, the target's placing and the three pressure gauges' peak, arrival and impulse (text, Tables 1-5, Figure 1)

redistribution.note: Transcribed from an open-access paper (CC BY 4.0), with citation.

coordinates: Ground at z = 0; the charge's centre at (0, 0, 0.7); x towards the plate, y across it, z up; metres.

ground.description: The ground's surface is not described; taken as flat.

obstacles.description: A steel plate carrying the gauges, placed as the paper's slabs were (1.2 m long and 0.5 m wide, upright, their centre 0.7 m above the ground; the long side taken vertical, as a gauge 0.3 m up implies). The plate's own size, thickness and frame are not stated.

tnt_equivalence.basis: the paper's stated equivalent, 10 kg of TNT; what it was matched to is not stated

charges.note: mass_kg is the stated TNT equivalent; the charge's own mass is not given separately.

scoring.note: No measurement uncertainty stated; one shot.

notes: The aluminium's contribution beyond its stated TNT equivalent is part of what this case tests: a code that takes the charge as 10 kg of TNT should say so.
The paper's slabs' displacements are not included: their supports are not described well enough to be modelled independently.
